title: Patient Financial Account — Schedule D, Payer Filing and Patient Liability Settings
content:
Schedule D gives, for each financial class of the Patient Financial Account, the settings that decide what reaches the patient after a claim goes to the payer.

- **Insurance-pending hold** — calendar days after the date of service during which the patient is not statemented for a charge whose claim is still pending with the payer.
- **Timely-filing limit** — the payer filing limit: calendar days after the date of service within which a claim must be filed with this class's payer; 0 means there is no payer to bill.
- **Balance billing permitted** — whether the patient may be billed above the payer-determined patient responsibility.
- **Advance notice of non-coverage required** — whether a signed advance notice of non-coverage (ABN or payer waiver) must be on file before a non-covered service is billed to the patient.
- **Secondary billed first** — whether a secondary coverage on file is billed before the remaining balance becomes patient responsibility.
- **Coordination-of-benefits response time** — calendar days the patient has to return a coordination-of-benefits questionnaire requested by the payer before the pended charge becomes patient responsibility.

| Financial class (tier) | Insurance-pending hold (days) | Timely-filing limit (days) | Balance billing permitted | Advance notice required | Secondary billed first | COB response time (days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Account | 60 | 180 | no | yes | yes | 30 |
| Self-Pay Account | 0 | 0 | yes | no | no | 30 |
| Medicare Part B Account | 30 | 365 | no | yes | yes | 45 |
| Medicare Advantage Account | 45 | 180 | no | yes | yes | 30 |
| Commercial HMO/EPO Account | 45 | 90 | no | yes | yes | 30 |
| Commercial PPO/POS Account | 45 | 180 | no | no | yes | 30 |
| High-Deductible Health Plan Account | 45 | 180 | no | no | yes | 30 |

Observations drawn from the table:

- The Self-Pay Account has a timely-filing limit of 0, so there is no payer to bill on that class, and it is the only class on which balance billing is permitted.
- The timely-filing limit is longest on the Medicare Part B Account (365 days) and shortest among insured classes on the Commercial HMO/EPO Account (90 days).
- The coordination-of-benefits response time is 45 days on the Medicare Part B Account and 30 days on every other class.
